title: Create a workflow that sends a prompt to an LLM
instructions: Create a workflow that sends a user-supplied prompt to an LLM and returns the model's response.

workflow_input.prompt: In one sentence, explain why the sky is blue.

criteria.title: Makes a call to an external LLM provider
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow sends data to an external LLM/model service and receives the model's generated response — through whichever step type its engine provides for this: a native model, llm or agent step, a provider/skill step, or a request to a provider's API. PASS: at least one step, of whatever type, is configured to call a model service capable of producing a chat-style completion, and the workflow uses what comes back. If the call is made as a raw request to the provider's API, that request is well-formed for creating a completion: it targets a completion-capable resource and uses the request method that resource accepts for creating one (POST). A native model step manages its own transport, so no endpoint or method is asserted for it. The specific provider is not asserted: any credible model service passes. FAIL: no step contacts any model service (the workflow returns a canned or locally computed value with no provider interaction), the call targets a resource incapable of producing a completion, or a raw API request uses a method the endpoint would reject (GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE).

criteria.title: A model/deployment identifier is specified
criteria.match_criteria: The step that performs the model call specifies a model or deployment identifier as a non-empty string — a model name, a deployment name, or the equivalent setting for its engine. PASS: any plausible model/deployment name for whatever provider the agent chose. No specific provider or model family is asserted: choosing them is the agent's judgment from the intent alone. FAIL: no model/deployment identifier appears anywhere in the produced workflow, the identifier field exists but is empty or whitespace-only, or the choice of model is left to an unstated default so a reader cannot tell which model the workflow calls.

criteria.title: Credentials are referenced by name, never as an inline literal
criteria.match_criteria: Every credential the workflow needs — for the model call and for any other authenticated request — is referenced by NAME through its engine's secret mechanism (a secret store, a named secret reference, an environment binding), so no credential value appears in the produced workflow. PASS: wherever a credential is supplied — an Authorization header, an API-key field, a key-bearing URL or body field, a step's provider configuration — it is populated from a named secret reference, optionally scheme-wrapped (a Bearer prefix) provided the token portion is itself the reference; a step whose engine binds the provider credential implicitly, with no credential field in the artifact at all, also passes. This criterion never asserts WHICH secret name is used, and a secret name that resolves to nothing in the judging environment is a warning upstream, never a failure here. FAIL: a plaintext credential appears anywhere in the produced workflow — a literal API key (for example a literal beginning sk-) or other live token in a header, in a URL query string or path, in a request body, or in a step's configuration.

criteria.title: Caller-supplied inputs reach the call by reference, not as literals
criteria.match_criteria: Each caller-supplied input genuinely reaches the step that consumes it, by reference rather than as a hard-coded literal: the `prompt` value is the request the model call sends, so the workflow produces a different exchange for different prompts. The reference may take whatever form the engine uses to read inputs and prior step outputs — a template expression, a variable binding, a step-output reference — and neither that syntax nor the provider's request-body schema (field names, message-array shapes) is asserted. What is asserted is that a different supplied value would produce a different call and therefore a different result. PASS: every declared input is read by reference at its point of use, as described above. FAIL: the prompt never enters the call, or it is embedded as a fixed literal (the workflow answers identically no matter what the caller supplies), or it is empty.

criteria.title: Workflow accepts a caller-supplied input named exactly `prompt`
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow declares and consumes a caller-supplied workflow input named exactly `prompt`, in whatever form its engine declares inputs (an inputs/parameters section, declared variables, or equivalent), and its behavior is driven by that input's value rather than by literals (the wiring asserted in C-004). PASS: an input with exactly that name is declared and read. FAIL: the input is declared under a different name (e.g. `query`, `userPrompt`), not declared at all, or replaced by a fixed literal — a rerun supplies values under exactly this name and cannot drive a workflow that reads different ones.

criteria.title: Workflow is structurally valid for its engine and ran to completion
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow is valid for the engine it was authored for and actually executed. PASS: all three hold — (1) it passes that engine's static validation — it parses, every step is well-formed, every referenced step, input, and secret resolves, and control flow proceeds from the entry point through every step to a successful terminal state with no unreachable or orphaned steps; (2) the rerun launched with the task's inputs ran to a COMPLETED state — not errored, halted, or timed out; and (3) what the run returns as its output is the deliverable the instructions describe — the model's response to the supplied prompt — rather than an intermediate value, a raw provider response envelope, or a status message. FAIL: the engine's validator rejects the workflow, the run errored or never completed, or the run's output is not the described deliverable.

criteria.title: The run output is a plausible LLM response to the supplied prompt
criteria.match_criteria: Judged against the RUN OUTPUT produced by executing the workflow with the supplied `prompt` input — not against the workflow JSON. There is no single correct answer; what is asserted is that the output reads as a plausible LLM-generated response to the supplied prompt: coherent text that is responsive to what the prompt asked. PASS: coherent generated text addressing the prompt. FAIL: the output is empty, an error message or stack-trace payload, raw request/response scaffolding with no generated text, a verbatim echo of the prompt with no answer, or content unresponsive to the prompt.
